messages:
Leah M.: quick heads-up 1: today's ask from a large retail pilot: when we spill to fallback region during Dedicated bursts, do we bill at source price, fallback price, or give a discount? need a recommendation by EOD so sales can answer.
Devon R.: My gut: bill at source price but mark as 'fallback-served' and offer a partial credit for involuntary routing. otherwise customers will request fallback to avoid higher regional costs.
Chen Y.: Implementation note: runtime already tags routed requests with region and model_variant. we can add a flag fallback_route=true and emit routed_latency_ms. billing can join on correlation_id. low dev cost.
Ops - Bea: Operationally we need to distinguish graceful fallback (no customer-facing impact) vs degraded fallback (higher latency or lower throughput). credits should only apply for degraded fallback. we should define thresholds: latency > +250ms or error_rate delta > 0.5% -> degraded.
Finance - Omar: From a pricing perspective, wholesale cloud cost matters. If fallback incurs higher infra cost, giving full refunds is risky. Proposal: degrade->50% credit of spilled_units, graceful->no credit. Also introduce a monthly cap of credits per tenant (e.g., 5% of committed units).
Leah M.: That aligns with sales expectations. Need product wording for pilot: "Fallback routing may occur to maintain availability. Customers only receive credits when fallback materially degrades performance or causes failed requests."
Devon R.: For GA telemetry: emit fallback_event {tenant_id, spilled_units, fallback_region, latency_delta_ms, error_delta_ppm, preempt_type}. that'll let billing decide.
Chen Y.: Also add a boolean 'was_preempt' if the fallback was caused by preemption vs regional outage. different treatment maybe.
Ops - Bea: Runbook addition: when fallback_event_rate > 0.3% over 10m for any tenant, auto-open incident and page oncall. Also post to #prod-fallbacks.
Finance - Omar: Pilot checklist for commercial terms: 1) fallback_event schema + dashboard 2) crediting rules codified and cap defined 3) product page copy + pilot contract appendix 4) test script simulating graceful vs degraded fallback 5) one pilot customer who agrees to billing behavior.
Leah M.: Timeline: can we get runtime flag + event in 1 sprint, dashboard in sprint 2, billing prototype with cap rules in parallel? target pilot in 6 weeks.
Devon R.: Yep. I'll own runtime flag and event schema (PR by Wed).
Chen Y.: I'll add the dashboard query and a simple Grafana panel (due next Tue).
Ops - Bea: I'll write the runbook step and setup the alert channel.
Finance - Omar: I'll draft the pilot appendix language and pricing cap table.
capacity-bot: Reminder: capacity roadmap sync on Fri 10:00.
Leah M.: Great. small product decision left: do we allow customers to opt-out of fallback routing entirely (i.e., fail instead of fallback)? sales says a couple customers will pay to opt-out. thoughts?
Devon R.: Technically trivial to add opt-out flag at tenant-level. risk: increased failed requests and oncall noise. opt-out should be gated behind a contract and higher commit.
Ops - Bea: If opt-out exists, require an explicit SLA waiver and add a monitor for failure spikes.
Finance - Omar: Charge a premium (suggest +20-35% depending on region cost delta).
Leah M.: OK we'll include opt-out as an add-on in pilot docs. If no objections, I'll lock this and file the product requirement ticket later today. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
